2. Apply monotonicity to positive square rootsThe complex operator algebra supplies its internal CFC instances, also in the trivial-space case. Monotonicity gives √(A_C²)≤√(B_C²); uniqueness of the positive roots identifies them with A_C and B_C. No commutation between A and B is used.AC2≤BC2⇒AC=AC2≤BC2=BC.Corresponding Lean step  have hAcNonneg : 0 ≤ Ac := (ContinuousLinearMap.nonneg_iff_isPositive Ac).mpr hAc
  have hBcNonneg : 0 ≤ Bc := (ContinuousLinearMap.nonneg_iff_isPositive Bc).mpr hBc
  have hSqLe : Ac*Ac ≤ Bc*Bc := by
    apply (ContinuousLinearMap.le_def _ _).mpr
    rw [hComplexDiff]
    exact hDc
  have hLe : Ac ≤ Bc := by
    have h := CFC.sqrt_le_sqrt (Ac*Ac) (Bc*Bc) hSqLe
    have ha : CFC.sqrt (Ac*Ac)=Ac := CFC.sqrt_unique rfl hAcNonneg
